articles.author: calvin-rook
articles.title: Granbull and Dracozolt lead a defensive-line board with distinct jobs
articles.dek: Twelve visible prospects separate into interior, edge and nose-tackle options; the combine adds context to the reported ranges.

body.text: University of Pyrite's Granbull and Turffield State's Dracozolt lead this defensive-line board. Granbull has the highest visible range among the twelve selected prospects at 65–93. Dracozolt follows at 64–92 and adds nineteen bench repetitions, a 4.82 forty and a 6.85 cone. The first choice depends in part on whether a club is seeking a defensive tackle or an edge player; the listed positions matter.

Dracozolt's movement tests make the edge evaluation particularly interesting. Solaceon's Heatmor has nineteen bench reps too, alongside a thirty-seven-inch vertical and a 6.80 cone, but a lower 53–81 range. Sonia's separate Heatmor runs 4.86 with a 6.79 cone and fourteen bench reps. Those are different combinations of reported range, strength and movement, not interchangeable versions of the same prospect.

The interior group has a wider gap between the leading candidate and the next name. University of Mossdeep's Loudred carries a 51–79 range at defensive tackle. Four listed nose tackles follow later on this board with narrower ranges. A team should compare those players against the job it actually needs filled rather than treating every defensive lineman as an equivalent answer to a sack total.

The divisional round offered several reminders that pressure can matter without establishing a complete scouting method. NeMarcus Tare recorded five sacks, EARTHQUAKE!!! four, and Derrat Brooks three. These are performances by established league players. They do not prove that a prospect with a similar species or a particular combine number will reproduce the same result. The college board below uses the visible scouting record for each individual.

No final draft order is assigned here, and the range endpoints are not secretly revealed current ratings. The judgments identify which prospects I would examine first and why. The next useful step for a club is to reduce uncertainty about its intended role, especially when choosing between a broad-range edge player and a more narrowly reported nose tackle.

prospects.name: Granbull
prospects.analysis: Granbull leads this board with a 65–93 visible range, a 5.01 forty and a 6.97 cone. University of Pyrite’s defensive tackle gives me the strongest reported range among these twelve.
prospects.concern: Fifteen bench repetitions do not establish a dominant strength advantage.
prospects.projection: First interior option on this board, with the broad range still requiring further evaluation.

prospects.name: Dracozolt
prospects.analysis: Turffield State’s Dracozolt pairs a 64–92 range with nineteen bench reps, a 4.82 forty and a 6.85 cone. I prefer this movement profile among the leading edge candidates.
prospects.concern: The range remains wide, and testing does not reveal a complete pass-rush repertoire.
prospects.projection: The leading defensive end here and a serious alternative to Granbull for a team prioritizing the edge.

prospects.name: Heatmor
prospects.analysis: Solaceon’s Heatmor has a 53–81 range, nineteen bench reps and a thirty-seven-inch vertical. The 6.80 cone is another reason to keep the prospect high.
prospects.concern: The reported range sits below the leading pair despite the attractive testing.
prospects.projection: An early alternative among this selected group if the top two are unavailable.

prospects.name: Carnivine
prospects.analysis: Agate’s Carnivine combines a 52–80 range with sixteen bench reps and a 6.96 cone. The profile earns a place near the top of the second group.
prospects.concern: A 5.03 forty offers less straight-line speed than Dracozolt.
prospects.projection: A developmental edge candidate whose specific role needs further evaluation.

prospects.name: Cranidos
prospects.analysis: Vermilion Metro’s Cranidos has the same 52–80 range and nineteen bench reps. Strength testing makes the comparison with Carnivine worth a close look.
prospects.concern: The 5.07 forty does not suggest the same movement profile as the fastest edge candidates.
prospects.projection: A second-group option for clubs weighing strength more heavily in their intended role.

prospects.name: Carnivine
prospects.analysis: South Paldea’s Carnivine is a separate prospect, with a 51–79 range, seventeen bench reps and a 5.00 forty. Keep the school and identity distinct from Agate’s player.
prospects.concern: The 7.02 cone is slower than several nearby alternatives.
prospects.projection: A middle-board edge option with a broad unresolved range.

prospects.name: Loudred
prospects.analysis: University of Mossdeep’s Loudred brings a 51–79 range at defensive tackle, with a 5.03 forty and a 7.00 cone. It is the next interior candidate after Granbull on this list.
prospects.concern: Fifteen bench reps do not remove uncertainty about the intended interior job.
prospects.projection: An interior alternative when the strongest range is no longer available.

prospects.name: Heatmor
prospects.analysis: Sonia’s Heatmor has a 50–78 range but a 4.86 forty and a 6.79 cone. That movement is the clearest reason to investigate a prospect below several peers by range.
prospects.concern: Fourteen bench reps give a different strength profile from Solaceon’s Heatmor.
prospects.projection: A movement-oriented edge option, with technical and role questions still open.

prospects.name: Geodude
prospects.analysis: Hauoli State’s Geodude is listed at nose tackle with a 50–50 range. The narrow reported interval distinguishes this evaluation from the wide-range defensive ends.
prospects.concern: A 5.23 forty, 7.18 cone and thirteen bench reps provide no basis for projecting unseen traits.
prospects.projection: A role-specific nose-tackle candidate evaluated on the known range.

prospects.name: Geodude
prospects.analysis: Oreburgh State’s Geodude has a 49–49 range and fifteen bench reps, with a 5.17 forty. The testing provides a useful comparison within the nose-tackle group.
prospects.concern: A fixed reported range should not be converted into an assumed development ceiling.
prospects.projection: A nose-tackle alternative with a slightly stronger bench result than the Hauoli prospect.

prospects.name: Geodude
prospects.analysis: University of Goldenrod’s Geodude also has a 49–49 range, with fourteen bench reps and a 5.18 forty. This is a third distinct player, not a repeated listing.
prospects.concern: The 7.13 cone is a testing result, not proof of game-level penetration.
prospects.projection: Another role-specific option in a tightly grouped nose-tackle set.

prospects.name: Roggenrola
prospects.analysis: Couriway’s Roggenrola closes the board with a 49–49 range and a thirty-one-inch vertical. The species and school distinguish the prospect from the three Geodude entries.
prospects.concern: Twelve bench reps and a 7.26 cone leave the testing case behind several nearby players.
prospects.projection: A later nose-tackle consideration when the role and remaining options justify it.
